page: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 dedicated physical core with 2 threads, operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Compute hardware includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

The instance includes 118 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage for temporary scratch space and caching needs, though it does not allocate complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution efficiency, where stress-ng single-core performance reaches the top 25% of measured instances. In contrast, aggregate parallel throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit, placing multi-core stress-ng, multi-core Geekbench, and PassMark CPU metrics in the lower 25th percentile.

Data throughput tests demonstrate average performance in single-threaded compression and decompression routines, as well as write memory bandwidth. However, large read operations, Redis SET operations at 2.95 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations benchmark in lower percentiles. The hardware architecture makes the D2ads_v6 cost efficient for lightweight general-purpose workloads, microservices, small web servers, and development environments that leverage single-threaded AMD execution along with local high-speed scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It provides 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 8.0 GB of memory, and 118 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU supports modern instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU execution but yields lower multi-core and database transaction throughput due to its entry-level two-vCPU capacity. Memory write speeds and single-threaded data compression remain balanced within median ranges, while small-model language inference handles lightweight tasks. Without bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance is positioned as a cost-efficient platform for containerized microservices, light web application serving, batch processing tasks, and test or development environments requiring fast local temporary storage.
